en.name: Tangyuan, frozen
en.summary: Frozen uncooked tangyuan keep 12 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, though a commercial bag's own printed date should win. The rule from Taiwan's food authority is blunt: refrigerate or freeze them, and never let them stand in the 7–60 °C range.
en.pantry: Do not leave tangyuan standing at room temperature at any point — not in the shopping bag on a long trip home, and not on the counter while the water comes to the boil. They are a wet, low-acid glutinous starch, often with a fat-and-sugar filling, and the official instruction is to keep them refrigerated or frozen and out of the 7–60 °C range entirely. Buy them last, carry them in an insulated bag, and get them into the freezer as soon as you are home.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is given for uncooked tangyuan, and the fridge is only for a short wait before they go into the pot. Cook them from frozen, get the centre above 70 °C (158 °F), and keep the water boiling for another minute or two after they float — floating means the surface is done, not the filling. Cooked tangyuan are a wet starch food: eat them hot, and if you must keep leftovers, refrigerate them below 5 °C (41 °F) for no more than a couple of days.
en.freezer: 12 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, a figure read across from frozen prepared meals; a commercial bag carries its own printed date and that date should win. Keep the bag genuinely hard at −18 °C and cook straight from frozen — thawed tangyuan collapse and the filling leaks out into the water. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe well beyond the window; what runs out is quality, as the skins crack and the filling dries.
en.thawing: Do not thaw. Drop them into boiling water straight from the freezer. A bag that has thawed should be cooked immediately rather than refrozen, and one that has thawed at room temperature should not be refrozen at all.
spoilage: Cracked, dry or split skins, which means the bag dried out or thawed and refroze.
Balls welded into one solid lump — the cold chain broke.
Filling leaking out of the skin before cooking.
A rancid smell from a sesame or peanut filling, whose oil is the first thing to age.
tips: Buy them last, carry them cold, and freeze them immediately.
Cook from frozen and keep boiling for another minute or two after they float.
Go by the printed date on a commercial bag rather than the general figure.
Handmade tangyuan freeze best spread on a tray first, then bagged once solid.

faq.q: How long do frozen tangyuan keep?
faq.a: 12 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, or the printed date on the bag if that is sooner.

faq.q: Do you need to thaw frozen tangyuan?
faq.a: No, and you should not. Cook them straight from frozen — thawed ones collapse and the filling leaks into the water.

faq.q: How do you know when tangyuan are cooked?
faq.a: Floating means only the surface is done. Keep boiling for another minute or two so the centre gets above 70 °C (158 °F).

zh.name: 冷凍湯圓
zh.summary: 未煮的冷凍湯圓在 −18 °C 下自購買日起可保有最佳品質 12 個月，不過市售包裝自己印的有效日期應該優先。食藥署的原則講得很直接：冷藏或冷凍，而且絕對不要讓它停留在 7～60 °C 之間。
zh.pantry: 任何時候都不要讓湯圓待在室溫——不管是提著在路上走很久，還是等水滾的時候先擺在檯面上。它是含水量高、低酸的糯米製品，而且常常包著油脂加糖的餡；官方的指示就是全程冷藏或冷凍，完全避開 7～60 °C 這個區間。請最後才拿、用保冷袋帶回家，一到家立刻進冷凍。
zh.fridge: 未煮的湯圓沒有給冷藏期限，冷藏只適合下鍋前的短暫等待。請從冷凍直接煮，讓中心超過 70 °C，而且浮起來之後再滾一到兩分鐘——浮起來只代表表面熟了，不代表餡熟了。煮好的湯圓是濕的澱粉類食物：請趁熱吃完；真的有剩，就冰在 5 °C 以下，而且不要放超過兩天。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下自購買日起 12 個月品質最好，這個數字是比照冷凍調理餐讀過來的；市售包裝上有自己的印製日期，那個日期應該優先。整袋要確實凍硬在 −18 °C，並且從冷凍直接下鍋——退冰過的湯圓會塌，餡也會漏到水裡。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全；先用完的是品質：外皮龜裂、內餡變乾。
zh.thawing: 不要解凍。直接從冷凍丟進滾水。整袋若已經解凍，請馬上煮掉，不要再凍回去；在室溫解凍過的更是絕對不能再冷凍。
spoilage: 外皮龜裂、變乾或裂開，表示整袋乾掉了，或曾經解凍又再凍。
整袋黏成一大塊——冷鏈斷過。
還沒下鍋餡就從皮裡漏出來。
芝麻或花生餡聞起來油耗；那些油脂是最先老化的東西。
tips: 最後才拿、低溫帶回家、立刻冷凍。
從冷凍直接煮，浮起來之後再滾一到兩分鐘。
市售包裝請以印製日期為準，不要只看一般數字。
自己搓的湯圓先在盤子上單顆攤開凍硬，再裝袋，才不會黏成一團。

faq.a: −18 °C 下自購買日起 12 個月品質最好；若包裝上的印製日期更早，以包裝為準。

faq.q: 冷凍湯圓需要先退冰嗎？
faq.a: 不需要，而且不應該。請從冷凍直接煮——退冰過的會塌掉、餡會漏進水裡。
浮起來只代表表面熟了。請再滾一到兩分鐘，讓中心超過 70 °C。
